title: The rhyme is broken. That's how you know it's human.
hook: There's a mistake in this poem. It's been there for 232 years.
specimen:
Tyger Tyger, burning bright,
In the forests of the night;
What immortal hand or eye,
Could frame thy fearful symmetry?
tell: 'Eye' and 'symmetry' don't rhyme. Blake let it fail rather than change the word. An AI swaps in a clean rhyme every single time — it cannot tolerate a broken one. The flaw is the fingerprint.
caption: AI never leaves a broken rhyme. Humans do it on purpose. 232 years and nobody fixed it.
cta: One specimen a day. Link in bio.
